APPLICATION 05 / ASSESS

Underwater Dam Inspection ROVs

See the upstream face without sending a diver.

Use an inspection ROV to record the condition of submerged dam faces, intakes, gates and spillway structures, with camera and sonar matched to the water conditions.

Home / Applications / Underwater dam inspection

Who this is for

Dam owners, hydropower operators, dam-safety engineers and inspection contractors.

Project inputs

  • Dam type, drawings and areas to inspect
  • Reservoir depth, expected visibility and flow at intakes
  • Launch position: crest, boat or pontoon
  • Required features, position reference and report format
Build a project brief

The short answer

Underwater dam inspection with an ROV records the condition of the upstream face, intakes, gates and toe without putting divers in the water. Choose the vehicle around depth, visibility and the features to record: a compact ROV such as the R-30 for visual work, or the higher-payload R-45 when sonar and positioning are required.

01

Define what the dam inspection must record

Typical targets include concrete deterioration, cracking, joint condition, seepage indicators, scour at the toe, debris against intakes and the condition of gates and trash racks. State which features matter and how findings will be referenced on drawings.

02

Plan for depth and visibility together

Reservoir water is often turbid near the bed. A camera-only inspection may work high on the face and fail lower down. Specify imaging sonar where visibility is poor, and confirm that it is integrated and recorded with the video.

03

Choose the vehicle by payload and handling

The R-30 is light and easy to deploy from a crest or boat; the R-45 carries an 8 kg payload for a fuller sensor package. Compare both with the actual sensors installed and the available launch position.

04

Reference every observation

Agree how depth, position along the face and heading will be logged, so that findings can be revisited and compared between inspections. Request a sample report and raw data before ordering.

05

Coordinate with operations and dam-safety procedures

Intake and spillway areas can carry flow. Agree isolation, exclusion zones and the inspection window with the owner, and record the recovery plan for snagging or loss of communication.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Frequently asked questions.

Can an ROV replace divers for dam inspection?

For many visual and sonar inspection tasks, an ROV removes the need to put people underwater, particularly in deep water or near intakes. Some hands-on tasks still need divers; define the scope first.

Which ROV suits dam inspection?

Start with the R-30 for compact visual inspection, or the R-45 when the inspection needs sonar, positioning or tools on board.
